title: Eviction oscillation adaptive-threshold and quarantine playbook
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary: After a capacity/regression incident on 2026-02-24 we observed repeated eviction oscillation across multi-tenant shards causing temporary OOMs and degraded p99 latency. The immediate mitigation (temporary global eviction rate cap) reduced impact but surfaced two persistent risks: (1) cross-tenant cache contamination via prefetch paths that increases eviction churn, and (2) eviction threshold thrashing when admission/load patterns change rapidly. This ticket defines a durable playbook: an adaptive eviction threshold with hysteresis plus a per-tenant quarantine/slow-path verification mechanism to prevent poisoning and reduce oscillation.

Root cause (brief): Concurrent prefetch + aggressive insertulence from several tenants caused hot entries to be evicted and reinserted in short intervals. The eviction score decay calculation did not account for rapid re-inserts, producing oscillating scores. Additionally, a rare checksum mismatch in the prefetch pipeline allowed stale/poisoned meta blobs to persist, increasing churn for affected namespaces.

Decisions made so far:
- Implement adaptive thresholding with exponential backoff/hysteresis rather than fixed thresholds.
- Introduce a tenant-scoped quarantine that routes suspicious inserts to a slow verification path for a short probation window.
- Add probabilistic per-entry checksums (8-bit salt+crc8) on write+read to detect corruption/poisoning quickly.
- Instrument new telemetry for eviction oscillation and quarantine events before full rollout.

Action items (owners and ETA):
1) Design: formalize adaptive threshold algorithm and hysteresis rules (owner: Miguel Torres; ETA: 2026-03-12).
2) Quarantine: implement tenant-scoped quarantine state machine and slow-path verification with sampling (owner: Priya Desai; ETA: 2026-03-19).
3) Checksum: add lightweight checksum tagging in prefetch write path + validation on read (owner: Kai Nguyen; ETA: 2026-03-15).
4) Telemetry: add metrics and alerts: eviction_oscillation_rate, tenant_quarantine_count, checksum_mismatch_rate, slowpath_verification_latency (owner: SRE - Jordan Lee; ETA: 2026-03-10).
5) E2E tests & chaos: introduce chaos test that injects re-insert storms and random stale-prefetch payloads (owner: QE - Lina Park; ETA: 2026-03-22).
6) Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% baseline with automated rollback on key alerts (owner: Miguel Torres; ETA: plan defined by 2026-03-20).

Telemetry & SLOs to track during canary:
- eviction_oscillation_rate <= 0.5% per shard
- checksum_mismatch_rate <= baseline*2 during rollout
- p95 token latency impact <= +5ms
- tenant_quarantine_count not growing > 2x baseline after 24h in canary

Runbook & fallback:
- If eviction_oscillation_rate exceeds 1% for >30m, automatically lower admission rate for affected shards and roll back adaptive-threshold flag.
- If checksum_mismatch_rate spikes unexpectedly, pause prefetch and trigger immediate forensic snapshot for affected tenants.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Checksum size vs performance: 8-bit reduces overhead but increases false negatives; 16-bit reduces false negatives but adds CPU. Proposal: start with 8-bit sampling on all writes and 16-bit for tenants tagged high-risk.
- Quarantine duration: default 30s may be too short for long-tail workloads; we will expose as a runtime knob.

- Incident timeline & notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INC/pages/2026-02-kvcache-oscillation
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Adaptive+Eviction+and+Quarantine+Design+Draft
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/4213 (adaptive threshold WIP), https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/4229 (quarantine state machine)
- Chaos tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/chaos-suite/issues/88

Milestones & timeline:
- 2026-03-12: finalize design and internal design review
- 2026-03-15: land checksum write+read validation with feature flag off by default
- 2026-03-19: land quarantine slow-path and unit tests behind feature flag
- 2026-03-22: complete QE chaos tests and green signal for canary
- 2026-03-24: begin 1% canary -> monitor 72h
- 2026-03-28: full rollout or rollback depending on canary metrics

Postmortem action items (close criteria):
- Adaptive threshold merged, canary completed, and rollout verified (owner: Miguel Torres).
- Telemetry dashboards and alerting in place (owner: Jordan Lee).
- Add automated regression test to CI that simulates eviction oscillation for future PR gating (owner: Lina Park).
- Update runbook and incident playbooks with recovery steps and links to new metrics (owner: SRE).

Updates: 2026-03-05 - Design review held; decision to prototype 8-bit checksum and 30s quarantine.
2026-03-08 - Telemetry PR merged; dashboards created in Grafana with baseline queries.
2026-03-10 - Checksum write path landed behind feature flag; initial unit tests passing.

Notes: Keep communications to enterprise customers who observed the incident: email drafted by PM with summary and mitigation commit ids. Coordination with Dedicated/Private teams required to ensure quarantine state persists across restarts for private deployments.
